title: Reveal, motion and highlight catalog
summary: Choose an animation for revealing, transforming or highlighting an entity and inspect it in a scene.

blocks.text: The creation directory contains 34 modules, including aliases and variants. Choose a reveal based on what the audience should understand: drawing a boundary explains construction, fading in communicates presence, and transforming a recurring symbol communicates continuity.

blocks.text: Each class has its own target restrictions and option type in the creation API reference. The catalog is a selection guide; refer to exact constructor contracts before substituting one animation for another.

Animation is the shared timing contract. StateAnimation supplies state interpolation; Sequential and Concurrent compose other animations. Focus on one of those branches to see its descendants, then open a type’s API to check options and behavior before choosing it for your scene.
The [complete class hierarchy](/class-hierarchy?type=Animation#explorer) also includes animation classes from the libraries.

MotionPath is a set of path-function factories for state position interpolation. Use arc, Bézier or other factories through AnimOptions.pathFunc. OrbitAnimation, SplineAnimation, SpiralAnimation, LissajousAnimation, ShakeAnimation and SpringAnimation are dedicated animation classes with separate geometry and dynamics options.

retiam/highlights contains boundary, backdrop, finish, material and motion emphasis animations. Circumscribe, CornerBrackets, Underline and BoundaryRipple derive geometry from bounds. MarkerSweep and BackdropFade steer attention; ShimmerSweep, SparkleBurst, FlashFinish and Flash mark milestones. ColorTint, PulseGlow, Blink, PopHighlight and WiggleHighlight animate temporary emphasis.

Overlay highlights can create and remove helper geometry, while target-mutating highlights restore captured state on completion. Use a fresh highlight object for each play and avoid simultaneous writers to the same target property.
Compare one easing function, then compare sequential and concurrent playback.
